experiment: Coverage reconstruction and edge-parameterized screen upscalers
decision: Keep bundled weights. Coverage heads fail flat-gray and halo checks. Edge-trained RGB improves fresh outline probes but does not establish a consistent visual upgrade and slightly regresses older groups.

training.coverage_auxiliary_loss: 0.3 alpha L1 + 0.1 alpha gradient + 0.1 color L1 + 0.1 geometry L1 + 0.25 fallback reconstruction + 0.05 detached oracle gate BCE

visual_review.method: Two independent gpt-6-luna sub-agents reviewed anonymous final panels without model names or numeric scores; root also inspected images. Tesseract was not used.

reviewer_1.overall: No consistent visual upgrade; most labels tied or uncertain.
reviewer_1.outline: Fine serifs, dots and thin strokes are cleaner in Target than every model.
reviewer_1.docs: Tight partial-glyph crop gives too little context to rank; slight fringing.
reviewer_1.scenes: All labels retain severe multicolor text smear/overlap compared with Target.
reviewer_1.cjk: All softer than Target; no reliable single winner.
reviewer_1.real_ui: Some apparent sharpness over bilinear, mild bright edge/ringing; no label winner.
reviewer_1.real_photo: No reliable label winner or verified recovered detail.

reviewer_2.overall: No consistent upgrade across the set; A-F mostly tied.
reviewer_2.outline: Punctuation and counters retained but all softer, thin strokes/ellipsis less clean than Target.
reviewer_2.docs: Very similar edges; fringing is also visible in reference, attribution uncertain.
reviewer_2.scenes: All models show substantially overlapping/merged text versus Target.
reviewer_2.cjk: All softer and less saturated than Target; thin strokes blur together.
reviewer_2.real_ui: All sharper than bilinear, no label-level winner or HR truth.
reviewer_2.real_photo: More texture than bilinear may be sharpening/noise; no defensible favorite.

root.overall: No clear perceptual upgrade over the shipped model in the inspected panels.
root.outline: Colored punctuation is still desaturated; fine glyph strokes remain softer than Target.
root.scenes: Every candidate preserves substantial source text smearing; sharpening does not recover target glyph separation.
root.cjk: Thin strokes remain fuzzy and color differs from target.
root.real_ui: All improve apparent edge definition over bilinear; candidate-to-candidate differences are small.

visual_review.review_correction: Reviewer 1 initially mixed four filename associations; root caught this, and reviewer re-opened those four files individually. This record uses the corrected associations.
limitations: Qualitative LLM reviews, not a human preference study or OCR measurement.
Small fixed sample set; some crops are clipped.
Real recordings have no HR truth.
CJK font exposure through original browser training data not ruled out.

root_observations: Visible diffuse halo/cloud around pale glyphs on dark background.
Three punctuation dots are too white compared with the colored target.
No obvious lost large counters in 0/8/B in these samples.
reviewer_1_summary: Mostly tied; weak preference D in case-7 and D/F in case-13, with low confidence.
All models miss ellipsis color in case-27.
All have a blue edge fringe in docs crop.
reviewer_2_summary: Some apparent extra sharpness has more halos.
Both ellipsis color and blue edge fringe remain wrong.
limits: Small fixed validation samples; some glyphs cropped at boundaries.
Visual preference is subjective, not OCR accuracy.
No architecture or training changes made in response to these early reviews.

limitations: One initialization and one documented optimizer restart; no statistical significance claim.
Original held-out datasets were examined in previous experiments.
Test hashes were frozen before this evaluation; no model tuning after inspecting final tests.
Four fresh conditions share each underlying render; group-average dB changes are not independent sample gains or pooled PSNR.
Coverage inference is fixed 2x and requires new heads; production shader tested only for compatible RGB-edge export.
GPU timing is fused PyTorch at 480x270 input; half precision here includes all layers, unlike the production shader.
No OCR or human preference benchmark.
